title: Browns vs. Steelers on Thursday Night Football: 2-1 AFC North rivals compete for division lead on Oct. 3
dek: The Cleveland Browns host the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4 Thursday Night Football with both teams at 2-1. The winner takes temporary first place in the AFC North. The game airs exclusively on Prime Video at 8:15 p.m. ET from Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Both teams enter at 2-1, with the winner claiming first place in the AFC North heading into the season's quarter-mark.
bottom_line: The Steelers' accelerating run game against a vulnerable Cleveland run defense offers the clearest path to victory on Thursday. Whether Watson can duplicate his fourth-quarter execution against a Steelers defense that has forced turnovers in consecutive games will determine whether the Browns can overcome their top-20 offensive rankings.
body:
The Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers meet Thursday night in a Week 4 matchup with playoff-season implications already emerging in the AFC North. Both teams carry identical 2-1 records into the matchup, and the winner will claim temporary first place in the division heading into the season's final quarter.
The game begins at 8:15 p.m. ET at Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland and airs exclusively on Prime Video, with announcers Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit and sideline reporter Kaylee Hartung.
The Browns won two straight games after an opening loss to Jacksonville. Per CBS Sports reporting, the Steelers enter at 2-1 after winning two one-possession games sandwiched around an embarrassment against New England.  Through Weeks 1 and 2, the Steelers gained 499 combined total yards (350 passing, 149 rushing) with 31 first downs, per CBS Sports. In Week 3, the Steelers gained 411 total yards (273 passing, 138 rushing) against the Bengals, the outlet reported.
Running back Jaylen Warren played 90 percent of snaps in Week 3 and tallied 20 touches for 176 yards, per CBS Sports. Rico Dowdle has been ruled out for the Steelers, making Warren the featured back. The Steelers' rushing yards have accelerated across the first three weeks, rising from 58 yards in Week 1 to 91 in Week 2 to 138 in Week 3, per CBS Sports. The Steelers average 4.3 yards per rush and allow opponents 305.7 yards per game (ranked 7th in the league), according to CBS Sports.
For the Browns, Deshaun Watson has completed 68.2 percent of passes at 7.2 yards per attempt with five touchdowns and one interception, per CBS Sports. Watson led game-winning fourth-quarter drives in each of the last two games, the outlet reported. The Browns threw for just 127 yards in their previous game, per CBS Sports reporting. The Browns rank 22nd in offense, averaging 266.3 yards per game, and 22nd in defense, allowing 344.3 yards per game, per CBS Sports. The team has struggled to run the ball, averaging 3.5 yards per carry (ranked 29th in the NFL), per CBS Sports. Quinshon Judkins leads the Browns backfield with 42 carries and has averaged 3.0 yards per carry, per CBS Sports. In Week 3, Judkins rushed for 70 yards on 18 carries against the Panthers, according to CBS Sports. Cleveland allows 4.5 yards per rush this season, per CBS Sports, while the Steelers allow 113 rushing yards per game (18th in the league), per the outlet.
The Browns have been outgained in each of their three games to date and have yet to record more than 17 first downs in any game this season, per CBS Sports. The Browns rank 28th in opponent pressure rate, per CBS Sports. The Steelers forced two turnovers in each of the last two games, per CBS Sports. The Steelers traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys late Wednesday night in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, per Sporting News reporting. Jalen Ramsey is listed as questionable with a wrist injury, per CBS Sports.
